Rachel — thanks for the overview in Friday's call. Before procurement signs off we need two concise artifacts for our security/compliance team: a failover sequence timeline (from detection to full service restore) and measured RPO samples for our key request paths (API token service, embeddings store, job-queue).

Specific asks:
- A short (one-page) timeline showing the sequence of actions during a failover, including detection thresholds, orchestration steps, and post-failover verification.
- RPO numbers measured during the last tabletop and any production DR rehearsals (include how RPO is determined for streaming WAL and KV cache).
- Any special custody/access procedures for KMS/HSM keys during failover (who has emergency access, how authorization is logged).
- Signed assertion we can attach to our SIG questionnaire (simple statement that RTO/RPO numbers below are measured values).

Can you get these over by EOD Wednesday so our security team can review before Thursday's procurement sync?

Thanks,
Laura

Laura — thanks, and understood. We can deliver a concise package that hits all four bullets. High-level answers here while we pull the detailed logs and signed attestation: 

- Failover timeline: detection (anometrics > 5% error rate or healthcheck cascade) -> controller failover decision (auto for infra-level incidents; manual for complex stateful failures) -> route draining -> KV warmstart on standby -> key unsealing -> verification probes -> full traffic cutover. Typical measured duration: targeted API path RTO ~ under 10m for partial service; full multi-region restore ~ 12–20m depending on state size.
- RPO for critical paths: embeddings store (S3+versioned snapshots) RPO ~ 0; job-queue (durable Kafka) RPO ~ 0–2s depending on replication lag; KV cache (in-memory prefix cache + write-ahead stream) observed RPO <= 2s in recent tabletop. We'll attach the log excerpts and a CSV of time-series samples.
- KMS/HSM custody: emergency unsealing requires 2-person approval from on-call security or designated ops manager; all actions audited via our KMS audit stream and recorded in the incident timeline. We will include the access roster and audit sample lines.
- Signed assertion: we can provide a one-paragraph signed PDF attestation (attached).

Ben/Marissa — can you drop the sequence CSV, kv timings, and the signed PDF into the shared S3 folder linked below? I will send a summarized one-pager for Tessera by EOD tomorrow (Wed).

Rachel
Rachel Kim
Head of Security Partnerships — Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: BCP details we need before procurement call

Added the artifacts to the bucket and included a short technical note below. Attached files: BCP_RPO_Test_Log.csv, kv_warm_timings.json.

Summary of measured events from tabletop (2026-09-10 rehearsal):
- Detection->Decision: median 34s (anomaly threshold + triage).
- Controller failover (orchestration + route update): median 3m 50s.
- KV warmstart (standby memcache population using WAL replay + prefix prefetch): median 2m 10s (95th pct 3m 5s).
- KMS unseal & key availability (HSM-backed): median 45s; requires 2 approvals via our approvals service, logged to audit.
- Service verification probes to full 99th pct latency SLA: median 6m 10s after cutover.

Observed RPOs (sampled across 12 trials):
- API token service (backed by durable DB + streaming replicator): 0–1s (typically sub-second).
- Embeddings store (object-store snapshots): near-zero (snapshots + versioning guarantee no data loss in test).
- Job-queue (replicated Kafka): 0–2s depending on tail lag at failure detection.
- KV cache: 0–2s, thanks to micro-checkpointing to WAL and synchronous write-through for critical keys.

Notes on measurement: logs annotated with event ids (evt-xxxx) so you can correlate sequence rows to timestamps. CSV contains columns: event_id, step, start_ts, end_ts, duration_ms, notes. kv_warm_timings.json contains per-shard warm sample traces.

Operational notes (custody & emergency process):
- HSM emergency access: 2-person approval; approvals recorded in KMS audit and mirrored to the incident timeline.
- Access roster: on-call ops lead + security on-call + engineering on-call for the product path.
- Post-incident review process: within 72h we publish a timeline and corrective items to the customer folder.

Attachments: BCP_RPO_Test_Log.csv (s3 link embedded), kv_warm_timings.json (shard array), small runbook excerpt included in the bucket (runbook-excerpt.md).

-ben
Ben Carter
Technical Account Lead — Redwood Inference
